before.q: The 1808 Rum Rebellion in Sydney overthrew which governor?
before.fact: It was the second time Bligh lost command to rebels: in 1789 his crew had seized HMS Bounty in a famous mutiny.

after.q: The 1808 Rum Rebellion in Sydney overthrew which governor?
after.fact: Bligh was no stranger to rebellion: in 1789 his crew had seized HMS Bounty in a famous mutiny.

reason: Rum Rebellion was not Bligh's second loss of command: his crew on HMS Director also mutinied in the 1797 Nore mutiny.

before.q: How many gold medals did China win at the 2024 Paris Olympics, level with the United States for the most?
before.fact: At Paris 2024 China's divers won all eight Olympic diving events, the first clean sweep of the sport at a single Games.

after.q: How many gold medals did China win at the 2024 Paris Olympics, level with the United States for the most?
after.fact: At Paris 2024 China's divers won all eight Olympic diving events, the first full sweep since the programme grew to eight events in 2000.

reason: China's 2024 diving sweep was not the first clean sweep of Olympic diving (the US won every diving event at e.g. 1932 and 1948); it was the first since the programme expanded to eight events in 2000.

before.q: Which Danish architect designed CopenHill, a waste-to-energy plant with a ski slope on its roof?
before.fact: The plant, opened in 2019, burns city waste to make electricity and heat for Copenhagen homes.

after.q: Which Danish architect designed CopenHill, a waste-to-energy plant with a ski slope on its roof?
after.fact: The plant began burning city waste in 2017 and its rooftop ski slope opened in 2019; it makes electricity and heat for Copenhagen homes.

reason: The CopenHill (Amager Bakke) plant started operating in 2017; only the rooftop ski slope/park opened in 2019.

before.q: Which Danish cyclist won the Tour de France in both 2022 and 2023?
before.fact: Vingegaard also finished second to Tadej Pogačar in 2021 and 2024.

after.q: Which Danish cyclist won the Tour de France in both 2022 and 2023?
after.fact: Vingegaard also finished second to Tadej Pogačar in 2021, 2024 and 2025.

reason: Vingegaard was also runner-up to Pogačar in the 2025 Tour, so listing only 2021 and 2024 was incomplete; asOf updated to 2025.

before.q: At Grenen, near Skagen at Denmark's northern tip, which two seas meet?
choices: The North Sea and the Baltic
The Wadden Sea and the North Sea
before.fact: Visitors can stand with one foot in each sea as the waves clash over the sandbar.

after.q: At Grenen, near Skagen at Denmark's northern tip, which two seas meet?
choices: The Wadden Sea and the North Sea
after.fact: Visitors can stand with one foot in each sea as the waves clash over the sandbar.

reason: Grenen is widely described (e.g. by tourism sources) as where the North Sea meets the Baltic, so that distractor was also defensible; replaced with a clearly wrong pair.

before.q: Who invented a raised-dot reading and writing system for blind people?
before.fact: Louis Braille lost his sight after an accident in his father's workshop at the age of three. He created his system as a teenager.

after.q: Who invented a raised-dot reading and writing system for blind people?
after.fact: Louis Braille lost his sight after an accident in his father's workshop at the age of three. He created his system as a teenager.

reason: Distractor Charles Barbier also devised a raised-dot ('night writing') system that was presented for use by blind people, so it was arguably also correct; replaced with Thomas Gallaudet.

before.q: Which striker overtook Thierry Henry in December 2022 to become France's all-time top goalscorer?
before.fact: Giroud retired from international football after Euro 2024 with 57 goals for France.

after.q: Which striker overtook Thierry Henry in December 2022 to become France's all-time top goalscorer?
after.fact: Giroud retired from international football after Euro 2024 with 57 goals for France. Kylian Mbappé broke his record at the 2026 World Cup.

reason: Mbappé overtook Giroud's 57-goal record at the June 2026 World Cup, so the fact implied Giroud is still the record holder; added that update.

before.event: The Lumière brothers hold the first paid public film screening

after.event: The Lumière brothers hold their first paid public film screening in Paris

reason: The Lumières' 28 Dec 1895 show was not the first paid public film screening (Latham's Eidoloscope in New York and Skladanowsky's Bioscop in Berlin charged admission earlier in 1895); reworded to 'their first'.

before.q: Opened in 1893, the Corinth Canal links the Gulf of Corinth with which other gulf?
before.fact: About 6.4 km long and only about 21 m wide at water level, the canal realised a project first attempted by Emperor Nero in 67 CE.

after.q: Opened in 1893, the Corinth Canal links the Gulf of Corinth with which other gulf?
after.fact: About 6.4 km long and only about 25 m wide at water level, the canal realised a project first attempted by Emperor Nero in 67 CE.

reason: The canal is about 24.6 m wide at water level (21.3 m at the bottom), not 21 m at water level.

before.q: Which Icelandic singer, formerly of The Sugarcubes, released the solo album 'Debut' in 1993?
before.fact: Björk released her first album at the age of 11 and later won Cannes' best actress award for 'Dancer in the Dark'.

after.q: Which Icelandic singer, formerly of The Sugarcubes, released the solo album 'Debut' in 1993?
after.fact: Björk recorded her first album at the age of 11 and later won Cannes' best actress award for 'Dancer in the Dark'.

reason: Björk's 1977 debut was recorded when she was 11 but released in December 1977, after she had turned 12, so 'released at 11' is inaccurate.

before.q: On 1 January 2024, Iran officially joined which group of emerging economies, alongside Egypt, Ethiopia and the UAE?
before.fact: The group is named after its first members: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.

after.q: On 1 January 2024, Iran officially joined which group of emerging economies, alongside Egypt, Ethiopia and the UAE?
after.fact: The name comes from its five members before 2024: Brazil, Russia, India and China, which founded it, and South Africa, which joined in 2010.

reason: BRIC's founding members were Brazil, Russia, India and China; South Africa joined in 2010, so it was not one of the 'first members'.

before.q: In March 2025, Iran qualified for which FIFA World Cup?
before.fact: It will be Iran's seventh World Cup and its fourth in a row since 2014.

after.q: In March 2025, Iran qualified for which FIFA World Cup?
after.fact: It was the seventh time Iran had qualified for a World Cup, and the fourth in a row since 2014.

reason: The 2026 World Cup has now been played, so "It will be" is stale; reworded to the qualification count, which holds either way.

before.q: In 2021, Italy banned large cruise ships from sailing into the historic centre of which city?
before.fact: The ban took effect in August 2021, shortly before UNESCO was due to consider adding the city to its list of World Heritage in Danger.

after.q: In 2021, Italy banned large cruise ships from sailing into the historic centre of which city?
after.fact: Approved in July 2021 to take effect that August, the ban came days before UNESCO was due to consider adding the city to its list of World Heritage in Danger.

reason: The ban was decreed on 13 July 2021 and took effect 1 August, after (not before) UNESCO's 15-23 July committee session considered Venice's endangered listing.

before.q: Which country knocked Italy, the reigning European champions, out of World Cup qualifying in a March 2022 play-off?
before.fact: Having lost a play-off to Sweden for the 2018 tournament, Italy missed two World Cups in a row for the first time.

after.q: Which country knocked Italy, the reigning European champions, out of World Cup qualifying in a March 2022 play-off?
after.fact: Having lost a play-off to Sweden for the 2018 tournament, Italy missed two World Cups in a row for the first time; a 2026 play-off loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina made it three.

reason: Italy has since missed a third straight World Cup, losing the March 2026 play-off final to Bosnia and Herzegovina on penalties.

before.q: In what year did Mexico achieve independence from Spain?
before.fact: The Army of the Three Guarantees entered Mexico City in September 1821, and its leader Agustín de Iturbide soon crowned himself emperor.

after.q: In what year did Mexico achieve independence from Spain?
after.fact: The Army of the Three Guarantees entered Mexico City in September 1821, and its leader Agustín de Iturbide was crowned emperor the following year.

reason: Iturbide did not crown himself; he was proclaimed by Congress and crowned in July 1822 (crown placed by Congress president).

before.q: Which ancient civilization carved the colossal stone heads found on Mexico's Gulf Coast?
before.fact: Seventeen colossal heads are known; the largest stand nearly 3 m (10 ft) tall and were carved from single basalt boulders.

after.q: Which ancient civilization carved the colossal stone heads found on Mexico's Gulf Coast?
after.fact: Seventeen colossal heads are known, each carved from a single basalt boulder; the largest stands about 3.4 m (11 ft) tall.

reason: The largest colossal head (La Cobata) is about 3.4 m tall, not under 3 m.

before.q: Which Mexico City stadium was chosen in 2024 to host the opening match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
before.fact: Estadio Azteca hosted the 1970 and 1986 World Cup finals, making it the first stadium set to stage matches at three men's World Cups.

after.q: Which Mexico City stadium was chosen in 2024 to host the opening match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
after.fact: Estadio Azteca hosted the 1970 and 1986 World Cup finals, and in June 2026 it became the first stadium to stage matches at three men's World Cups.

reason: The 2026 opener (Mexico 2-0 South Africa, 11 June 2026) has now been played, so "set to" is outdated.

before.q: Which fossilised resin was dug from Northland fields in the 1800s and exported to make varnish?
before.fact: Thousands of gumdiggers, many from Dalmatia in today's Croatia, worked the northern gumfields.

after.q: Which fossilised resin was dug from Northland fields in the 1800s and exported to make varnish?
after.fact: Thousands of gumdiggers, many from Dalmatia in today's Croatia, worked the northern gumfields.

reason: Kauri gum is itself a copal resin (often called 'kauri copal'), so the distractor 'Copal' was defensibly correct; replaced with Shellac.

before.q: Which team won the women's Rugby World Cup final at Eden Park in November 2022?
before.fact: The Black Ferns beat England 34–31 in front of more than 42,000 fans, a record crowd for a women's rugby match.

after.q: Which team won the women's Rugby World Cup final at Eden Park in November 2022?
after.fact: The Black Ferns beat England 34–31 in front of more than 42,000 fans, then a record crowd for a women's rugby match.

reason: The 42,579 crowd was a record only until the 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup final at Twickenham drew about 82,000.

before.q: At the October 2023 election, Te Pāti Māori won how many of the seven Māori electorates?
before.fact: Its electorate wins outstripped its party vote, creating an overhang that took Parliament to 123 seats.

after.q: At the October 2023 election, Te Pāti Māori won how many of the seven Māori electorates?
after.fact: Its electorate wins outstripped its party vote, creating a two-seat overhang; with an extra seat from the Port Waikato by-election, Parliament grew to 123.

reason: Te Pāti Māori's overhang was two seats (to 122); the 123rd seat came from the Port Waikato by-election overhang.

before.q: What is the capital of Norway?
before.fact: Oslo sits at the head of the Oslofjord, and nearly half of its area is forest and protected nature.

after.q: What is the capital of Norway?
after.fact: Oslo sits at the head of the Oslofjord, and more than half of its area is forest and protected nature.

reason: Forest (Marka) and protected nature cover well over half of Oslo municipality (commonly cited as about two-thirds), so 'nearly half' understated it.

before.q: Which South African singer was known worldwide as "Mama Africa"?
before.fact: Makeba's 1967 hit "Pata Pata" made her one of the first African musicians to top international charts.

after.q: Which South African singer was known worldwide as "Mama Africa"?
after.fact: Makeba's 1967 hit "Pata Pata" made her one of the first African musicians to score a major international chart hit.

reason: Pata Pata peaked at No. 12 on the US Billboard Hot 100, so it did not "top" international charts.

before.q: The 16th-century glazed tiles decorating Topkapı Palace and the Blue Mosque were mainly made in which town?
before.fact: İznik potters perfected a vivid "tomato red" glaze that was famously hard to reproduce.

after.q: The 16th- and 17th-century glazed tiles decorating Topkapı Palace and the Blue Mosque were mainly made in which town?
after.fact: İznik potters perfected a vivid "tomato red" glaze that was famously hard to reproduce.

reason: The Blue Mosque (built 1609-1616) was decorated with early-17th-century İznik tiles, so calling all the tiles 16th-century was inaccurate.

before.q: In 1932, which town gained the region's first airfield, a stop on Imperial Airways' route to India?
before.fact: Passengers stayed overnight at the Al Mahatta fort, which is now a museum of aviation.

after.q: In 1932, which town gained the Trucial Coast's first airfield, a stop on Imperial Airways' route to India?
after.fact: Passengers stayed overnight at the Al Mahatta fort, which is now a museum of aviation.

reason: Bahrain's Muharraq airfield also opened in 1932 on the same Imperial Airways route, so 'the region's first' was overstated; narrowed to the Trucial Coast.

before.q: The Wars of the Roses were fought between the House of Lancaster and which other royal house?
before.fact: The wars ended in effect at Bosworth in 1485. The body of Richard III, the last king to fall there, was found under a Leicester car park in 2012.

after.q: The Wars of the Roses were fought between the House of Lancaster and which other royal house?
after.fact: The wars ended in effect at Bosworth in 1485. The body of Richard III, the last English king to die in battle, was found under a Leicester car park in 2012.

reason: 'the last king to fall there' wrongly implies other kings died at Bosworth; Richard III was the only one, and the last English king to die in battle.

before.q: Gold found at Sutter's Mill in 1848 sparked a famous rush to which present-day state?
before.fact: About 300,000 "forty-niners" poured in, and California went from territory to statehood in just 1850.

after.q: Gold found at Sutter's Mill in 1848 sparked a famous rush to which present-day state?
after.fact: About 300,000 "forty-niners" poured in, and California became a state in 1850 without ever being an organized US territory.

reason: Fact implied California was a US territory before statehood; it went straight from Mexican cession (1848) to statehood (1850) with no organized territorial stage.
